p:cNvPr.descr: an image showing biological tethers. The top image depicts dihydrolipoyl transacetylase (E2), and has lipoate on the left, where S bonds right to S (both in red box). S bonds up and left, the up and right, and then down and right to a blue binding line. The second S binds up and right to this blue bonding line. This line moves to the right and goes up, down, up, down, and at the next up point is double bonded to O, which bonds down and right to N, which begins the lys residue. N binds up, down, up, down, then up to H over C, which bonds down and right to N over H and up and right to C, which double bonds up to O. Just below this, the pyruvate carboxylase image is depicted. It begins with biotin, which begins with O double bonded down to the top point of a pentagon (second point). From the left point, clockwise, is HN (in a pink box) and the third point is NH. The bottom side of this pentagon also shares the top side of a pentagon just below it. The fifth point of this pentagon is S, which bonds up and right to a blue bonding line, which extends right and goes up, down, up, down, and up again. At the point, O double bonds to it, then bonds down and right to N, where lys residue begins, as described above. In the last diagram, it highlights acyl carrier protein. FOr beta-mercaptoethylamine, HS (in a red box) bonds down and right, then up and right, then down and right (blue bond lines) to N over H, which bonds up to a double bond to O, where pantothenate begins. O then bonds down, then up, then down to N over H, which bonds up to where O is double bonded to the point. This continues to go right and down to the next point where OH is bonded. The blue bond line from that point goes up to the point where it is bonded (in black) to CH3 up and to the left, and to CH3 up and to the right. From this point it continues down (in blue), then up to O, where O bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and bonds right to O, which bonds to Ser.
